> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR

> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/rest/src/import-template.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **19** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 4b8f597ba357ba45c7b4b4a4504c78b2a079f123` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `e003539fddf28c6a73ab9c8f1303ce7a7e725f55` — the merge of head `3d3bafba2842e08acbfc9de0409d368a1e30ba9e` into base `4b8f597ba357ba45c7b4b4a4504c78b2a079f123`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin e003539fddf28c6a73ab9c8f1303ce7a7e725f55 && git checkout e003539fddf28c6a73ab9c8f1303ce7a7e725f55
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 4b8f597ba357ba45c7b4b4a4504c78b2a079f123 3d3bafba2842e08acbfc9de0409d368a1e30ba9e && git checkout -B drift-repro 4b8f597ba357ba45c7b4b4a4504c78b2a079f123 && git merge --no-ff 3d3bafba2842e08acbfc9de0409d368a1e30ba9e

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 4b8f597ba357ba45c7b4b4a4504c78b2a079f123
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 4b8f597ba357ba45c7b4b4a4504c78b2a079f123` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## 席位核对 · ACCEPT

`domain:cli` seat 2 (#22648) · `os-justin` · session `session_01LmjU2x1faLZ39DVTFyVca6` · 2026-10-20T23:05Z · head `3d3bafba2842e08acbfc9de0409d368a1e30ba9e` · claim `6302401259` → report `6303744014`. No contract face (`Clause-②: no`: only a boolean cell's words follow the caller's locale), so no review of record is owed.

| Check | Reading |
|:--|:--|
| Shape | Draft, base `main`. First line `Fixes #24945`; `Clause-②: no` line-initial. Assignee `os-justin` = the card's. One changeset, `@objectstack/rest: patch`. |
| Surface | 10 files, +367 / −30: `export-format.ts`, the export route in `data-action-routes.ts`, `import-template.ts` (an import moved to `@objectstack/core` so the two modules do not import each other), `rest-server.ts`, one new pin file, four existing pins, and the changeset. `rest-server.ts` was outside the claim. **This seat adds it to the surface**: the route host gains `resolveI18nService` / `extractLocale` (both already on `RestServer`), and `rowsToCsv` gains an optional `booleanWords`. `rowsToCsv` is not exported from `@objectstack/rest`. Without it, the header and the cells could not read one locale. `check-governed-merges.mjs --pr 24998`: NOT governed. |
| Mechanism | Read in the diff. The route resolves the i18n service once and reads `extractLocale(req, i18n)`. It takes `templateText(locale).booleanWords` (`import-template.ts`, the one table), and hands the same service to `translateMetaItem` (its existing optional `i18nService` parameter), so the header and the cells cannot disagree. csv, xlsx and json all pass the words. The formatter's no-words default is `templateText(undefined)`, the English pair, with no second literal table. |
| Evidence | 5 of 11 pins red on `main` (`1,Wren Halvorsen,是,否` under an English header). Each language's csv and xlsx re-imports as `[true,false]` / `[false,true]`. Two ablations (the locale hand-off; the i18n service handed to `extractLocale`) each red the pins they name; both restored hash-equal. The Chinese fixtures name a `zh-CN` caller, and the recorded template-route bytes stay identical. The rest package in full: 307 files / 6165 tests. |
| Gates | Local: 68/68 derived families and the 10 Declared WIDE population families exit 0, 0 UNRUN; `pnpm lint` exit 0. Check-runs on this head (38, latest per name), read at this act: 14 success, 7 skipped, 17 `in_progress`. Landing waits on all of them. |

**Accepted deviations:**
- `rest-server.ts`, as above.
- The dispatch's suggested ablation direction could not hold: a dropped locale falls to the English pair, so the zh pins go red. The en pin's red reading is red-on-`main`.
- #2481's plan listed 是 / 否 before the export read any locale. It carries no maintainer ruling, and #2916 made export/import follow the caller.

**Acceptance notes (one line each):**
- With no i18n service and no locale, the header shows the authored labels while the cells read `yes` / `no`. The import template behaves the same way, and a deployment whose i18n service declares a default resolves both halves to it.
- json boolean cells remain display strings, now in the caller's words, as the formatting layer's design has them.

**Landing:** through the merge queue by this seat once every check on this head reads `success` (or an expected skip).
